newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt GDP growth five pct in 1996/7 - minister.
newsitem.headline: Egypt GDP growth five pct in 1996/7 - minister.

text.p: The Egyptian economy is expected to grow five percent in real terms this financial year, which ends on June 30, Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib said in an interview published on Friday.
The estimate is lower than those given by Economy Minister Nawal el-Tatawi this month and by Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri earlier in the financial year. Both predicted 5.7 percent.

"The rate of real growth in gross domestic product in 1996/7 has reached 4.5 percent and it is expected to reach five percent as a result of the large expansion in industrial production, which has grown 8.5 percent, and because of the great activity in transport and tourism and the progress in the financial sector," Gharib told the government newspaper al-Ahram.

The minister said he expected inflation during the rest of this financial year to stay at around 5.7 percent, the rate recorded in the year to the end of January. Inflation fell to 5.4 percent at the end of February.
He said the government's budget deficit in this financial year would be the equivalent of about one percent of GDP -- about the same as previous estimates.
